caption: for odd $n$, an $n$-cycle is even — $(1\,2\,3\,4\,5)$ decomposes into 4 transpositions
for even $n$, the full $n$-cycle would be odd, so the second generator is one point shorter: $(2\,3\,4)$
at $n = 3$ the two generators coincide, so there is only one
$A_3$ is cyclic of order 3 — the identity and the two 3-cycles
$A_1$ is the trivial group — $1!/2$ isn't even an integer, so this is a base case, not the formula
$A_2$ is trivial too — $S_2$'s only even permutation is the identity
